candidates.title: A library run's cost card closes on the package's set price, so its capital recovery line takes the whole NPV gap
candidates.area: cost card: proforma_worker.tea_breakdown for library.run, CostWaterfall
candidates.statement: For a library plant's run the TEA breakdown is read at the product's set price (the worker hands no solved price to the table reader) and Capital recovery is sales less AOC at that price, so whenever the TEA solves another price the line takes the NPV gap: cornstover with a person's feed price of 0.08 USD/kg shows Capital recovery 0.0902 USD/kg where the plant's capital and IRR give about 0.226, and the composed cellulosic_ethanol_v0, every stream and unit equal to cornstover's, shows 0.286 against cornstover's 0.2249.
candidates.contract: core/openferment_core/workers/proforma_worker.py:427 "capitalRecovery": ("Capital recovery", "TEA.sales less TEA.AOC: the return on and of the capital, and its tax"); src/components/figures/CostWaterfall.tsx:1 "What the price is made of"; workers/proforma_worker.py:510-514 (tables) "Where the flowsheet solved a price, the product carries it while every table is read" (a Proforma run reads its card at its solved price, a library run at the list price)
candidates.reproCommand: bash /home/user/openFermentUI/bughunt/notes/H4/scripts/repro.sh H4-01 (scripts cornstover_feedprice.py and compare_plant.py; the screen: node scripts/costcard.mjs <origin> h4p <run id>)
candidates.expected: Lines that close on the run's base-case price, 0.7945 USD/kg, with Capital recovery the return at the TEA's IRR: sales at 0.7945 USD/kg less AOC, about 41.75 M USD/yr, 0.226 USD/kg; the same plant at the same price giving the same card whether it is cornstover or cellulosic_ethanol_v0.
candidates.observed: Run 4fb3f640b39e3955 rendered in Chromium: 'Base case, every input at its value: 0.7945 USD per kg of ethanol'; rows Main feedstock 0.3794, Other materials 0.2005, Utilities -0.0605, Fixed operating 0.0493, Capital recovery 0.0902, closing row 'Price the lines are read at 0.6588'. cellulosic_ethanol_v0 at its default (run e7efa2505b4633de, solvedPrice 0.658813642, packagePrice 0.7198608115): Capital recovery 0.286; cornstover (bfda026530692adc): 0.2249, every other line equal.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/workers/library_plants.py:818 (_Module.parts passes "price": None, so tea_breakdown reads the product at its set price) with core/openferment_core/workers/proforma_worker.py:459 ("capitalRecovery": sales - aoc)
candidates.evidence: Direct biorefineries route (direct_plant.py) and the service agree on every TEA number to ten digits (cmp-cornstover.txt, cmp-cev0-vs-cornstover.txt: 118 streams, 68 units equal); the cards differ only in the price the breakdown is read at. Reproduced twice, once on a fresh database by repro.sh.

candidates.title: A library run that sets any value re-simulates unsettled, so a value equal to the default moves the price in the fifth digit
candidates.statement: When a library run sets any value the worker simulates the built plant a second time, and simulate() settles only a composed flowsheet, so cornstover with its feedstock price set to the library's own default prices ethanol at 0.6588285541 USD/kg with an NPV of -20,477 USD where the run that sets nothing prices 0.658813642, a difference of 2.3e-5 on a run whose basis states ten significant digits.
candidates.contract: docs/api/engines.md:615 "A library thing's precision is ten significant digits (`rtol` 1e-9)"; docs/decisions/ADR-004-biosteam-adapter.md:120-125 measures the unsettled second simulation (0.6588285541) and settles the composed flowsheet for it alone
candidates.expected: The same plant at the same values prices one price to the precision its basis states: 0.658813642 USD/kg.
candidates.observed: solvedPrice 0.6588285541 and NPV -20477.5 USD (run 73dd9fcbad97f341) against 0.658813642 and 0 (run bfda026530692adc); capital recovery 41,573,039.7 against 41,575,770.25 USD/yr.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/workers/library_plants.py:782-784 (apply, then simulate) with :711-712 (simulate settles only when p.flowsheet is set)
candidates.evidence: Measured twice (main service and a fresh database). A study that moves a library input by a small step reads this re-simulation's 2.3e-5 as the input's effect.

candidates.title: fermOS's mass balance flags a fed-batch whose cells take up nothing as not closing
candidates.statement: The closure is the gap divided by the sugar consumed, so a fed-batch with no uptake (closed form: V = V0 + F t and every concentration diluted, which the run meets within 1.2e-6) reports closure 1.0 from 8.5e-5 g of integrator error (1.5 with a feed of water), flags 'The mass balance does not close: 1 against 1%.' and says the rate laws do not hold together.
candidates.contract: core/openferment_core/kinetics.py:88-96 "9. The mass balance is checked ... Both are invariants of the equations ... the check catches a wrong right-hand side ..., never integrator error"; fermos.py note "The check catches a wrong rate law, not the integrator's error"
candidates.reproCommand: bash /home/user/openFermentUI/bughunt/notes/H4/scripts/repro.sh H4-04 (scripts kinetics_cases.py case 7, kinetics_more.py case C)
candidates.expected: massBalance ok true and no flag: the equations hold exactly (X, S, P and V match the closed form within 1.2e-6 relative).
candidates.observed: {closure: 1.0, ok: false, note: 'Sugar consumed, 8.45561e-05 g ... outside the 1% closure, so the rate laws or their parameters do not hold together'}; flags ['The mass balance does not close: 1 against 1%.']; feed of water: closure 1.5, consumed -1.5429e-05 g.
candidates.evidence: Seven other hand cases close to 1e-15..4e-7; a fed-batch with growth closes to 2e-7.

candidates.title: A batch with μmax zero is refused as one whose sugar never runs out, though β or maintenance use it up
candidates.statement: Asked to run until the sugar runs out, a batch with μmax 0 is refused because 'the sugar never runs out', yet with β 0.1 g g-1 h-1, X0 2 g/L, Yp/s 0.5 and S0 20 g/L the sugar falls at 0.4 g/L/h and runs out at 49.95 h, which the same family reports when a run length is named.
candidates.contract: core/openferment_core/kinetics.py:58-61 "'Until the sugar runs out' integrates over horizons doubling from 1/μmax ... and a run whose sugar stops falling (growth stopped at Pmax, or by the second nutrient) is refused in words"
candidates.expected: A run that ends at the run-out hour, 49.95 h, or a refusal only for a sugar that stops falling.
candidates.observed: 422 'μmax is zero, so the cells never grow and the sugar never runs out: name a run length'; with t_end 60 h: sugarRunsOutH 49.95000000025453, end S 0, P 10.

candidates.title: ethanol_glucose_v0 takes a titre at harvest that its beer never reaches
candidates.statement: The titre input sets only the batch time (titre over productivity), and the beer's ethanol follows from the feed's glucose and the yield, so a run with titre 70 g/L, feed 150 g/L and yield 0.45 makes beer at 61.83 g/L and is priced on a 35 h batch; nothing holds the titre to what the feed can make, so a titre above feed x yield is priced too.
candidates.expected: Beer at the titre at harvest the run names (70 g/L), or a refusal in words when the feed and the yield cannot make it.
candidates.observed: readBack beerEthanolGPerL 61.830259604809335, batchTimeH 35.0 (run eb4ad3a1fce70fa2), base price 1.0536688973 USD/kg.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/flowsheets/ethanol_glucose_v0.py:219 (b.R1.tau = titre / productivity) with no check of titre against feed_glucose_conc x yield
candidates.evidence: The same holds for custom_train_v1, which takes the same inputs.
